sections.heading: Why garage door websites lose jobs they should win
sections.intro: Most garage door searches are urgent and made on a phone. These are the gaps we see most often.

items.title: The phone number is hard to find
items.body: When a door is stuck or off its track, a number hidden in a menu sends the customer to the next company.

items.title: Repair, installation and openers are mixed together
items.body: A broken spring and a new door are different jobs. Without clear paths for each, visitors leave unsure you handle theirs.

items.title: The service area is unclear
items.body: If visitors cannot quickly tell whether you cover their town, they do not enquire.

items.title: No easy way to request a quote
items.body: Not every customer wants to phone. A short request form captures the ones who would rather write.

items.title: Trust is left to chance
items.body: Licence and insurance details, reviews and past work belong where customers look for reassurance.

items.title: Slow or dated on mobile
items.body: A site that loads slowly or looks out of date undercuts the quality of the work you actually do.

items.title: Click-to-call on every page
items.body: Your number stays one tap away on phones, so urgent customers can reach you without searching.

items.title: Separate paths for repair, installation and openers
items.body: Clear service sections so each visitor lands on the job they need, with a call or quote request beside it.

items.title: Emergency and scheduled service options
items.body: Give urgent and planned jobs their own route, so each customer knows what to do next.

items.title: A home for reviews, licences and project photos
